correctness.rationale: The actual RESULT.md defines the nonabsorbing longest-prefix automaton A for an arbitrary word w, including borders and zero-probability irrelevant letters. Its upper-Hessenberg zero pattern and fixed one-step superdiagonal make the (0,m-1) inverse entry a triangular cofactor z^(m-1) times the product of the first m-1 letter probabilities. Thus E[z^(T-m)]=p_w/det(I-zA), including m=1. Every block of m letters hits the target with conditional probability at least p_w, so ||A^m||∞<=1-p_w and rho(A)<1. Normalization at z=1 gives det(I-A)=p_w, and -logdet(I-zA)=sum_k tr(A^k) z^k/k converges absolutely; all diagonal entries of A^k are nonnegative. This proves exact nonnegative finite Lévy intensity, not merely an approximate or finite-prefix law. When p_w=1 the process is deterministic zero. Kumulants via exponential moment analyticity are sums k^r nu_k. Inspected word_wait_checker.py constructs KMP automata, rational Newton identities and independent short-word enumeration; listed 498 word tests and 365 exhaustive short checks are supplemental, not a universal proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Count approximations cannot imply exact divisibility of first hit. Recurrences for a restricted word class also cannot prove a universal arbitrary-overlap word assertion.
